extracted.intended_audience: Users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (algebraic geometers / singularity theorists) who use the alexpoly.lib, arcpoint.lib, classify.lib libraries
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for SINGULAR library procedures (alexpoly.lib, arcpoint.lib, classify.lib) describing usage, assumptions, returns, and examples for computing invariants and performing operations on (plane) curve/hypersurface singularities.

rubrics_metrics.name: totalmultiplicities
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: totalmultiplicities(INPUT); INPUT poly or list. INPUT is either a REDUCED bivariate polynomial defining a plane curve singularity, or the output of hnexpansion(f[,"ess"]), or the list hne in the ring created by hnexpansion(f[,"ess"]), or the output of develop(f) resp. of extdevelop(f,n), or a list containing the contact matrix and a list of integer vectors with the characteristic exponents of the branches of a plane curve singularity, or an integer vector containing the characteristic exponents of an irreducible plane curve singularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: list L of three integer matrices. L[1] is the incidence matrix of the resolution graph (diagonal entries are weights; a negative entry corresponds to the strict transform of a branch). L[2] has for each vertex a row and for each branch a column; entry [i,j] is the total multiplicity of the j-th branch along the exceptional divisor corresponding to i. L[3] contains the (strict) multiplicities similarly. Note: The total multiplicity is the multiplicity with which the exceptional divisor occurs in the total transform. Example usage given; if unsure whether INPUT is reduced, use squarefree(INPUT) as input; or better compute the Hamburger-Noether expansion via hnexpansion and use that as input.

rubrics_metrics.name: alexanderpolynomial
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: alexanderpolynomial(INPUT); INPUT poly or list. INPUT same possibilities as totalmultiplicities (REDUCED bivariate polynomial, hnexpansion output, develop/extdevelop output, contact+charexp list, or an integer vector of characteristic exponents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create: a ring with variables t, t(1), ..., t(r) where r is the number of branches and ordering ls over the ground field; the ring contains the Alexander polynomial (alexpoly), the zeta function of the monodromy (zeta_monodromy), and alexfactors (factors with multiplicities). Return: a list ALEX where ALEX[1] is the created ring. Notes: to use ring type def ALEXring=ALEX[1]; setring ALEXring; or ring(ALEX,"ALEXring"); access alexpoly, zeta_monodromy, alexfactors. Example given. If you need Hamburger-Noether expansion for other purposes, compute with hnexpansion first. If unsure whether INPUT is reduced, use squarefree(INPUT).

rubrics_metrics.name: semigroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: semigroup(INPUT); INPUT poly or list. INPUT same possibilities as above (REDUCED polynomial, hnexpansion output, develop/extdevelop output, contact+charexp list, or integer vector of characteristic exponents of an irreducible plane curve singularity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: a list with three entries. The first and second are lists v_1,...,v_s and w_1,...,w_r of integer vectors such that the semigroup of the plane curve defined by INPUT is generated by v_1,...,v_s,w_1+k*e_1,...,w_r+k*e_r where e_i denotes standard basis vector and k runs through non-negative integers. The third entry is the conductor. Notes: if output is zero the curve has one branch and is regular; in the reducible case generators may not be minimal. If unsure whether INPUT is reduced, use squarefree(INPUT). Example and cross-reference to invariants() for irreducible case.

rubrics_metrics.name: proximitymatrix
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: proximitymatrix(INPUT); INPUT poly or list or intmat. INPUT same possibilities as previous procedures or the resolution graph (output of resolutiongraph or first entry in totalmultiplicities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: list of three integer matrices. First is the proximity matrix (entry i,j is 1 if the infinitely near point corresponding to row i is proximate to that of row j). Second is the incidence matrix of the resolution graph; diagonal in row i is -s-1 if s is number of points proximate to that infinitely near point. Third is the incidence matrix of the Enriques diagram: rows correspond to infinitely near points (including strict transforms of branches), diagonal gives level, entry i,j is -1 if row i is proximate to row j. Note: if input is a smooth curve output are three 1x1 zero matrices. Definitions reference Eduardo Casas-Alvero book. If Hamburger-Noether expansion needed for other purposes, compute with hnexpansion and use that; if unsure whether INPUT reduced, use squarefree(INPUT). Example usage and relationships N = -transpose(P)*P, and relations to multiplicities (M = P*TM).

rubrics_metrics.name: multseq2charexp
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume: The input is an intvec containing the multiplicity sequence of an irreducible plane curve singularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: an intvec which contains the sequence of characteristic exponents of the irreducible plane curve singularity. Example: multseq2charexp(intvec(2,1,1)) -> 2,3.

rubrics_metrics.name: charexp2multseq
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: charexp2multseq(v), v intvec. Assume: v contains the characteristic exponents of an irreducible plane curve singularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: intvec, the multiplicity sequence of the plane curve singularity. Note: If the curve singularity is smooth then the multiplicity sequence is empty and zero is returned. Example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: charexp2generators
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: charexp2generators(v), v intvec. Assume: v contains the characteristic exponents of an irreducible plane curve singularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: intvec, the minimal set of generators of the semigroup of the plane curve singularity. Example provided. Cross-references: invariants(), resolutiongraph, totalmultiplicities.

rubrics_metrics.name: charexp2inter
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: charexp2inter(contact,charexp), contact matrix, charexp list. Assume: charexp contains integer vectors of characteristic exponents of branches and contact is their contact matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: intmat, the matrix of intersection multiplicities of the branches. Example shows computing intersection matrix from invariants and then recomputing via charexp2inter(contact,charexp).

rubrics_metrics.name: charexp2conductor
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume: v contains the characteristic exponents of an irreducible plane curve singularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: int, the conductor of the plane curve singularity. Note: If the curve singularity is smooth, the conductor is zero. Examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: charexp2poly
rubrics_metrics.description: Inputs: v an intvec containing the characteristic exponents of an irreducible plane curve singularity; a a vector containing the coefficients of a parametrization given by x(t)=t^v[1], y(t)=a(1)t^v[2]+...+a[n-1]t^v[n] (entries of a are of type number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: A polynomial f in the first two variables of the basering such that f defines an irreducible plane curve singularity with characteristic exponents v. Note: Entries in a should be numbers and v should be the sequence of characteristic exponents to get sensible result. Example provided; cross-reference to multseq2charexp, multseq2generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: tau_es2
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: tau_es2(INPUT); INPUT poly or list. INPUT same possibilities as previous alexpoly procedures (REDUCED bivariate polynomial, hnexpansion output, develop/extdevelop output, contact+charexp list, or intvec of characteristic exponents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: int, the equisingular Tjurina number of f (codimension of the mu-constant stratum in the semiuniversal deformation of f, where mu is the Milnor number). Note: The equisingular Tjurina number is calculated with the aid of a Hamburger-Noether expansion, which is the hard part of the calculation. Recommendation: if Hamburger-Noether expansion is needed elsewhere, compute it first with hnexpansion and use that as input. If unsure whether INPUT polynomial is reduced, use squarefree(INPUT). Examples given.

rubrics_metrics.name: arcpoint.lib overview / truncation of arcs
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview: Library arcpoint.lib — Purpose: Truncations of arcs at a singular point. An arc is given by a power series in one variable t; truncating at order i means cutting t-powers > i. The set Tr(i) of arcs truncated at order <bound> is constructible. Procedures implement algorithm of Lejeune-Jalabert for computing relevant locally closed sets contributing to truncations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures compute constructible sets of truncated arcs up to a given order; relies on algorithm and provides routines for manipulation (nashmult, removepower, idealsimplify, equalJinI, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: nashmult
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: nashmult(f,bound); f polynomial, bound positive integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create: allsteps (list containing all relevant locally closed sets up to order <bound> and their sequences of Nash Multiplicities) and setstep (list of relevant locally closed sets obtained from sequences of length bound+1). Return: a ring — original basering with additional variable t and coefficients up to t^<bound>. Example provided showing setring R; allsteps etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: removepower
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: removepower(I); I ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: an ideal defining the same zeroset as I: if any generator of I is a power of one single variable, replace it by the respective variable. Example: I = x3, y+z2-x2 -> removepower(I) -> x, -x2+z2+y. See also idealsimplify.

rubrics_metrics.name: idealsimplify
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: idealsimplify(I,m); I ideal, m int. Assume: procedure is stable for sufficiently large m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: an ideal defining the same zeroset as I: replace generators of I by the generator modulo other generating elements. Example shows reducing x3 to x when m large. Cross-reference removepower and equalJinI.

rubrics_metrics.name: equalJinI
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: equalJinI(I,J); (I,J ideals). Assume: J contained in I and both I and J have been processed with idealsimplify before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: 1 if I=J, 0 otherwise. Example demonstrates behavior with simple ideals. See idealsimplify for preprocessing.

rubrics_metrics.name: basicinvariants
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: basicinvariants(f); f = poly. Compute: Compute basic invariants of f: an upper bound d for the determinacy, the Milnor number mu and the corank c of f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: intvec: d, mu, c. Example provided. From classify.lib.

rubrics_metrics.name: classify (Arnold classifier)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: classify(f); f=poly. Compute: normal form and singularity type of f with respect to right equivalence as given in Arnold, Gusein-Zade, Varchenko.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: normal form of f, of type poly. Remarks: This classify is beta; set init_debug(n) (0<=n<=10) to get intermediate info. The proc creates global objects starting with @. Use with Singular >=1.0.1. Note: classification may apply Morse-splitting and other steps; examples and debug traces shown. Send bugs to author. Cross-reference many internal functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: corank
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: corank(f); f=poly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: the corank of the Hessian matrix of f, integer. Remark: corank(f) equals number of variables occurring in the residual singularity after applying morsesplit to f. Example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hcode
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: Hcode(v); v=intvec.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: intvec, coding v according to number of successive repetitions of an entry. Examples illustrate coding behavior (e.g., 1,2,3,4,4,4,... -> 1,1,1,7,1,1,1).

rubrics_metrics.name: init_debug
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: init_debug([level]); level=int.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute: Set the global variable @DeBug to level. @DeBug used by debug_log to decide when to print messages. init_debug() reports only changes of @DeBug. Useful as trace-mode; n may range 0..10, higher gives more info. Examples show debug messages at various levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: internalfunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: internalfunctions();
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: nothing, display names of internal procedures of classify.lib. Lists many helper functions used by the classifier and the Morse-splitting lemma; helpful to understand internals or debugging.

rubrics_metrics.name: milnorcode
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: milnorcode(f[,e]); f=poly, e=int (default e=1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: intvec, coding the Hilbert function of the e-th Milnor algebra of f (i.e., basering/(jacob(f)^e)) according to proc Hcode. Note: a big second argument may result in memory overflow. Examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: morsesplit
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: morsesplit(f); f=poly. Compute: apply the splitting lemma (generalized Morse lemma) to f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: Normal form of f in M^3 after application of the splitting lemma. Example shows extracting residual singularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: quickclass
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: quickclass(f); f=poly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: Normal form of f in Arnold’s list. The proc tries to determine normal form by invariants mainly via Hilbert function of the Milnor algebra; no coordinate change needed. Example demonstrates classification to D[4].

rubrics_metrics.name: singularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: singularity(t, l); t=string (name of singularity), l=list of integers/polynomials (indices/parameters of singularity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute: get the singularity named by type t from the database; l provides indices/parameters. Return: normal form and corank of the singularity named by type t and its index(es). Note: the dbm database NFlist.[dir,pag] must be present; if not, run MakeDBM first. Examples given for various named types.

rubrics_metrics.name: A_L (A L)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: A L(f); f poly OR A L(s); s string name of singularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute: In case 1 compute via milnorcode the class of f and return the normal form found in the database. In case 2, get the normal form from the database for the named singularity. Return: normal form. Examples show retrieving normal forms like c2+a3+ab5+b8.

rubrics_metrics.name: normalform
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: normalform(s); s=string.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: Arnold’s normal form of singularity with name s (pulls from database). Example: normalform("E[13]") -> c2+a3+ab5+b8.

rubrics_metrics.name: debug_log
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: debug_log(level, li); level=int, li=comma separated "message" list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute: print messages if level >= @DeBug. Useful for user-defined trace messages. Example usage with init_debug shown. See init_debug for controlling @DeBug.

rubrics_metrics.name: swap
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: swap(a,b);
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: b,a for input a,b (any type). Example: swap("variable1","variable2") -> variable2 variable1.

rubrics_metrics.name: modality
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: modality(f); f poly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: the modality of the singularity (integer). Example provided. Part of classify.lib.

rubrics_metrics.name: complexSingType
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: complexSingType(f); f poly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: the type of the singularity as a string (e.g., D[4]). Example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: prepRealclassify
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: prepRealclassify(f); f poly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: a list containing the modality of the singularity and the type of the singularity as a string. This procedure is needed in realclassify.lib to avoid classify() being called more than once. Example provided.
